body:
# the contributor audit: exposed-face deletion and circuit protection


`candidate c9f582e034f0948d`. I read the
full note and re-read the critical-cap and quantile-cover dependencies.
No below-target descent conclusion is proved by this result.

The positive-depth candidate and circuit existence assumptions are
justified for actual finite convex fiber families by the archived
boundary-zero-cap argument and directional-cap compactification.
The new finite-tilt argument strictly excludes vertical active caps
while counting every whole boundary fiber. Moving an active cap through
its candidate preserves its mass. Balanced through-candidate margins
sum to zero on the ENTIRE anchor plane, giving the exact cover.

After deletion, a surviving anchor ball supplies uniform strictly
decreasing quantiles near the old mass. A negative weighted threshold
shift permits a further small decrease of common cap mass without
losing the cover. This bounds every candidate in that fiber, rather
than only a chosen moved center. Finitely many other fibers retain
their old strict gaps. Thus the exact criterion implies descent of
the actual full maximum depth.

The right threshold slope correctly includes proper sections and
supporting facets with the body inside the cap; the left slope
instead includes outside supporting facets. Both are positive from
the anchor. The two one-sided section limits follow from convex
interpolation and compactness. The removed mass at a shifted threshold
can be replaced by the fixed-threshold incidence ONLY under the
explicit small-slab interaction condition. Under that condition the
signed inverse formula follows, including zero shift when incidence
equals beta. The nonsmooth binary-incidence ratio uses the correct
two slopes and has a positive denominator.

For a cap-sign-stable exposed face, compactness gives one common
incidence neighborhood and eliminates the moving-threshold interaction.
The face trim is admissible only while every original fiber remains
positive and the removed mixed mass tends to zero; the note states
these conditions and does not use a whole-fiber vertical excision.
An exposed measured point has a positive gap from all other compact
fibers, so a sufficiently small trim affects just its own fiber.

The protection quantifiers are correct: failure of the universal
statement supplies one strictly profitable circuit at EACH of the
finitely many deepest bases; their common trim then works simultaneously.
An empty admissible circuit family makes the protection statement
vacuous, as explicitly acknowledged. Adding a plane is permitted at an
unrestricted minimum, but not automatically in a fixed-N-plane class.

For an exposed polytope vertex, the removed body is exactly a scaled
bounded truncated tangent cone for sufficiently small scale. Its mass
is t^d times the cone volume. A threshold slab of width O(epsilon)
inside that O(t)-diameter region has volume O(epsilon t^(d-1)), which
is o(epsilon) for d>=2. Hence boundary-passing cap incidences are
retained exactly as tangent-cone fractions. For a nonpolytopal exposed
point the diameter tends to zero, yielding the same interaction
estimate and subsequential finite incidence limits. The d1 exception
is correctly left to the exact quantile criterion.

The square-corner certificate uses a genuine covering triple. Its
three exact areas and final normalized decrement are correct. Products
in the integer coordinates retain the same covering caps, and the
central base has depth1/2 before trimming. The moved plane exposes
a face in the product, not necessarily one point, as the note states.

Finally the protected-layer example has2^(n-1) independent binary
layers, each of absolute maximum3|Q|/2. The normalized full value
is2^-n, with every fiber below the2^-n heavy-fiber threshold. Every
single exposed-point trim leaves another whole layer unchanged and
strictly reduces total mass, so maximum depth increases. This example
does not lie below the OC target. It correctly blocks any descent
claim based only on nonsimplicity and absence of a heavy fiber.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
